overall: Board violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating via email on June 1 about an acting library director; scheduling info was not a violation; the chair's unilateral-action claim was declined.

allegations.summary: Chair allegedly acted unilaterally on matters within the Board's jurisdiction, including the selection of an acting library director.
allegations.key_passage: Because the selection of an acting library director falls outside the scope of the Open Meeting Law, we decline to review an allegation that it was done improperly.

allegations.summary: Members allegedly deliberated outside a posted meeting by email on June 1 about who would serve as acting library director during the director's leave.
allegations.key_passage: When the Board discussed this topic via email, it violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Scheduling information included in the June 1 emails was examined for whether it constituted deliberation.
allegations.key_passage: Inclusion of scheduling information in the emails of June 1 did not violate the Open Meeting Law, as such information is explicitly excluded from the definition of deliberation.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.

Release within 30 days of any written communication, including emails and text messages, exchanged by Board members about who would serve as acting library director during the director's medical leave.
All Board members attend a training by the Division of Open Government on the Open Meeting Law within 90 days.
Certify to the AG's office that the Board has complied with the above orders.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
